$comment: Patterns are paired with `not: {pattern: \n}` because JsonSchemaValidator evaluates them as Ruby regexps, where ^ and $ match at any line break. Rejecting newlines keeps the anchors meaning start and end of string under both Ruby and ECMA regexp semantics, and matches Gitlab::PathTraversal, which treats a newline in a path as a traversal attempt.

path.description: Path to the skill's SKILL.md file. The parent directory is the skill, so consumers can resolve co-located resources such as references/ alongside it.

git_ref.description: Branch the skill was published from. Always the project's default branch.

blob_sha.description: Git object ID of the SKILL.md blob. Content-addressed, so it doubles as provenance and as the change-detection key. Deliberately not the commit SHA: the commit moves on every unrelated push, which would mint a new item version on every publish.

commit_sha.description: Commit that last changed SKILL.md. Provenance only, never a change-detection key: change detection compares blob_sha, so recording the commit does not mint a version on unrelated pushes.

author_name.description: Git author name from that commit. Recorded because git attribution is a name and an email, which need not correspond to a GitLab user. When they do, the version's created_by is set as well and takes precedence.

license.description: Optional Agent Skills specification field, cached from the front matter so the catalog can show it without reading the blob.

compatibility.description: Optional Agent Skills specification field describing environment requirements.

allowed_tools.description: Optional Agent Skills specification field, spelled allowed-tools in front matter and renamed here to match the snake_case of the rest of the definition. Experimental in the specification.
